Method of Attack: Double-extortion ransomware attacks involving data theft and file encryption on Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi servers
Encrypting files using Salsa20 (NoEscape) or AES (Avaddon) with RSA-encrypted keys
Deleting Windows Shadow Volume Copies and backups
Terminating security, backup, web, and database processes and services to unlock files for encryption
Using Windows Restart Manager API to close processes or services that keep files open
Threatening public release or sale of stolen data if ransom is not paid
Deploying ransomware after gaining Windows domain admin credentials and spreading laterally
Discoverer: Michael Gillespie (ID-Ransomware creator and ransomware expert)
Indicators of Compromise: Unique 10-character file extension appended to encrypted files
NoEscape Tor negotiation site with personal ID, ransom amount in bitcoins, test decryption, and chat panel
Data leak site listing victims and leaked data sizes

Commands deleting shadow copies and backups (e.g., SHADOWCOPY DELETE /nointeractive, wmic SHADOWCOPY DELETE /nointeractive, wbadmin DELETE SYSTEMSTATEBACKUP -deleteOldest, vssadmin Delete Shadows /All /Quiet)
Processes terminated including 360doctor, QBW32, mysqld, sqlservr, outlook, tomcat, and others
Windows services stopped including QBCFMonitorService, RTVscan, VMAuthdService, sqlservr, veeam, vmware-converter, and others
